successCriteria.description: `npm run seed` (which runs `knex seed:run` against the development environment) completes without error and inserts the demo dataset: one MANAGER employee, one EMPLOYEE employee (managerId -> manager), the `annual` and `sick` leave types, an ACTIVE leave policy per type, a current-period leave_balance per employee per type, and two or three leave_requests in SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED states.

Running `npm run seed` a second time against an already-seeded database inserts no duplicate rows and deletes nothing — every seeded row is detected by its composite key (employees by email/employee_number, leave_types by code, leave_policies by stable seed id, leave_balances by employee_id+leave_type_code+period_start+period_end, leave_requests by employee_id+leave_type_code+start_date) and skipped.

The seeded employees' `password_hash` values are minted via `bcrypt.hashSync('demo-password', 10)` (the same call `AuthService` verifies with), so `POST /auth/login` succeeds for `manager@example.com` and `employee@example.com` with the shared password `demo-password`.

Balance-counter consistency holds: for each seeded leave_balance, `pending_days` equals the sum of `requestedDays` over SUBMITTED requests for that (employee, leave type, period) and `used_days` equals the sum over APPROVED requests — both derived from the seeded requests, never hardcoded independently.

Every seeded leave_balance's `period_start`/`period_end` are produced by `periodContaining(employee.hireDate, policy.accrualPeriodMonths, new Date())` (never a hand-written date), and every seeded leave_request's `requested_days` is produced by the shared `requestedDays(startDate, endDate)` helper.

`knexfile.js` exposes a `seeds` directory only for the `development` environment (and shared `base` if appropriate); `production`, `smoke_pg`, and `test` have no seeds config, so the seed never runs as part of `migrate` or the smoke/test paths.

constraints: The seed service MUST import canonical enums/helpers only from their declared public entry points: `LeaveTypeCode`, `LeaveStatus`, `EmployeeRole`, `requestedDays` from `src/shared/types`; `periodContaining` from `src/shared/date`; `LeavePolicyStatus` from `src/modules/policy` (the public entry point, never a bare `'ACTIVE'` string).

The demo password literal MUST be hardcoded as `const DEMO_PASSWORD_LITERAL = 'demo-password';` with a one-line comment stating it is demo data — never read from an environment variable. Both demo accounts (`manager@example.com`, `employee@example.com`) share this password.

Use the exact canonical field names from the architecture (camelCase in TypeScript model logic, snake_case DB columns in knex insert objects) — do not rename, split, add, or omit fields. Date columns are inserted as `'YYYY-MM-DD'` strings derived via `.toISOString().slice(0,10)`.

The seed entry `seeds/001_demo_data.js` MUST register ts-node (`require('ts-node/register')`) and delegate to the seed service, because `tsconfig.json` has `rootDir ./src` / `include ["src"]` and excludes the `seeds/` directory from compilation.
The seed writes directly through the knex instance (standard knex seed mechanism), not through application repositories — no new repository interfaces are introduced.
outOfScope: The dev-runner (`scripts/dev.js` + `npm run dev`), the web `vitest run` fix, and README documentation are Phase 2–4 and out of scope for this phase.
No API endpoints, routes, controllers, RBAC, audit-log writes, or transaction boundaries are introduced — the seed is a development-only data loader with no runtime API surface.
The seed must never run as part of `migrate` and must not be wired into `production`/`smoke_pg`/`test` environments.

entityInvariants.invariant: Exactly one MANAGER and one EMPLOYEE are seeded; the EMPLOYEE's `managerId` references the MANAGER's id; both carry a `passwordHash` minted via `bcrypt.hashSync('demo-password', 10)` and `employmentStatus` ACTIVE.

One balance row per (employee, leave type) for the CURRENT accrual period, with `periodStart`/`periodEnd` derived via `periodContaining` anchored on `hireDate`; `pending_days`/`used_days` are derived from the seeded requests' statuses (SUBMITTED→pending, APPROVED→used), never hardcoded independently.

Two or three requests in distinct lifecycle states (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED), each with `requestedDays` computed via the shared `requestedDays` helper and `status` set to a canonical `LeaveStatus` value.
One ACTIVE policy per seeded leave type (`annual`, `sick`), each with a stable seed id and `status = LeavePolicyStatus.ACTIVE`.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Re-running must be a no-op for already-seeded rows (skip, never duplicate or delete); it must not throw on a second run against an already-seeded database.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the canonical `requestedDays(startDate, endDate)` helper (inclusive whole-day UTC count) for every seeded request's day count — never re-derive it locally.

Reuse `periodContaining(anchor, accrualPeriodMonths, date)` (and `startOfUtcDay` where needed) from the shared date entry point to derive balance period boundaries — matching exactly what `BalanceService.getCurrentBalances` computes, so seeded balance rows satisfy the `findByKey` unique tuple.

Match the canonical `Employee` field shape (id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, role, managerId, department, hireDate, terminationDate, employmentStatus, passwordHash) and the snake_case `employees` columns from the initial migration when inserting.
Match the canonical `LeavePolicy` field shape (including `status: LeavePolicyStatus`) and the snake_case `leave_policies` columns; import `LeavePolicyStatus` from the policy public entry point.
Match the canonical `LeaveRequest` field shape (14 fields incl. `cancelledBy`/`cancelledAt`) and the snake_case `leave_requests` columns from the initial migration when inserting.
Match the canonical `LeaveBalance` field shape and the snake_case `leave_balances` columns (including the unique `(employee_id, leave_type_code, period_start, period_end)` tuple) when inserting.
Match the canonical `LeaveType` field shape (code, name, requiresApproval, maxConsecutiveDays, isPaid) and the snake_case `leave_types` columns when inserting the `annual`/`sick` types.
Mint password hashes with `bcrypt.hashSync(plaintext, 10)` — the exact call `AuthService.login` verifies with via `bcrypt.compare` — so the demo accounts can authenticate.

integrationPoints.why: The `seeds: { directory: './seeds' }` block must be added so `knex seed:run` discovers `seeds/001_demo_data.js`.
The `"seed": "knex seed:run"` script must be added so `npm run seed` invokes the seed against the development environment.
Source of the canonical `LeaveTypeCode`, `LeaveStatus`, `EmployeeRole` enums and the `requestedDays` helper the seed imports.
Source of `periodContaining` (and `startOfUtcDay`) used to derive current-period balance boundaries.
Public entry point re-exporting the module-local `LeavePolicyStatus` enum the seed must import (never a bare `'ACTIVE'` string).
